items.title: new way to integrate AsyncLocalStorage
items.body:
This PR addresses the feature request here https://github.com/trpc/trpc/issues/6870

## Problem Statement

Currently, integrating AsyncLocalStorage with tRPC requires:

1. Manual context passing
2. Global procedure middleware wrapping

This creates unnecessary boilerplate for a common need.

## Solution

Add optional `asyncStorage` to runtime config that automatically wraps all procedures to improve developer experience.

### Why Runtime Configuration?

- **Architectural Fit**: Async context is a runtime concern, not request context
- **Backward Compatible**: Optional parameter maintains existing behavior
- **Clean DX**: Single configuration point vs middleware wiring

## Implementation

### Propagation Path

1. Run time config → Root config → Procedure builder → Resolver → Procedure caller
2. Preserves full type safety throughout
3. inject context into the storage for type safety

## Key Considerations

### Performance

- Minimal overhead (AsyncLocalStorage is optimized for this)
- Only active when configured
- short-circuit pattern  run the async storage on the same index as middleware chain

### Advanced Use Cases

- **Nested Procedures**: Automatically inherit storage
- **Overrides**: Still possible via manual `.use()` wrapping with not passing asyncStorage as runtime configuration
- **Middleware**: Runs within storage context

## Usage Example

```tsx
const storage = new AsyncLocalStorage();
const t = initTRPC.create({
  asyncStorage: storage 
});

// Any procedure automatically has context storage
const router = t.router({
  getUser: t.procedure.query(() => {
    deepFunction(); // Can access context via storage.getStore()
  })
});

```

## Alternatives Considered

1. **Context-Based**: Rejected - wrong abstraction l[a](http://async-context-management.md/)yer
2. **Plugin System**: Overkill -  focused use case
3. **Global Middleware**: existing solution before this with .use on a procedure  

## Final note :

- I have also updated the documentation and added example for this, as new concept in docs docs/server/[a](http://a[sync-context-management.md](http://sync-context-management.md/)/)sync-context-management.md

## ✅ Checklist

- [ x] I have followed the steps listed in the [Contributing guide](https://github.com/trpc/trpc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x ] If necessary, I have added documentation related to the changes made.
- [x ] I have added or updated the tests related to the changes made.

items.title: feat: support lambda response streaming
items.body:
Closes #4474 

## 🎯 Changes

This PR adds support for [AWS Lambda response streaming](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/introducing-aws-lambda-response-streaming/). Response streaming is only supported by Lambda Function URLs, **not** by API Gateway.

I decided to add a new adapter `awsLambdaStreamingRequestHandler()` instead of changing the existing adapter `awsLambdaRequestHandler()` because it makes this an opt-in feature and avoids accidental breaking changes. Moreover, Lambda Function URL uses the API Gateway V2 event format and doesn't support V1, so having a new adapter that only supports V2 avoids this issue. We could also integrate response streaming into the existing adapter and enable it with an option `streaming: true`, but the returned handler function signature is different from usual Lambda handler signature.

I added a new example `examples/lambda-url` to demonstrate this feature. Response streaming is not supported by serverless-offline, so it can't be tested locally. I left my own deployed Lambda Function URL in the code so that you guys can quickly test event without your own AWS account. This should obviously be removed later on. 

I didn't update the docs yet, but I can do this if you approve the PR and we decide if this should be a separate adapter (as it is now) or be integrated into the existing one.

EDIT: See comment https://github.com/trpc/trpc/pull/6680#issuecomment-2782111826 for latest update

items.title: feat(next/app-dir): `contextCache` to control context values to add to `cacheTag`
items.body:
Closes: #5455

## 🎯 Changes
This change allows a user to specify `contextCache` method in the `experimental_nextCacheLink`, which lets one select the values from the context that should be considered when a `cacheTag` is generated.

It also changes the way `cacheTag` is generated, taking care of the fact that the `cacheTag` cannot be longer then 256 characters, thus instead of stringifying input values, it will form a sha-256 hash of those.
